children: A classified Space Force payload put Falcon 9 on Thursday's launchpad for its 104th mission of 2026. Space Exploration Technologies

, the space-launch and satellite-network company, climbed 1.8% to approximately $150.25. A successful flight from Vandenberg would lift SpaceX's total launch count across all vehicles to 106 this year.

That relentless pace follows Sunday's Falcon 9 mission, which carried 27 Starlink satellites into orbit. SpaceX's share of global launches has eased to roughly 49% from more than half last year, but the company remains the heavyweight champion in payload mass. A classified military customer adds another powerful signal: Falcon 9 is not merely feeding Starlinkit is critical national-security infrastructure.

The valuation picture looks far less comfortable. The graphic gives SpaceX a GF Score of just 15 out of 100, with financial strength standing out while profitability, growth, value and momentum remain weak. Meanwhile, about 2.3 billion shares could become eligible for trading before year-end, potentially expanding the current 2.6 billion-share float by roughly 88%. The rockets keep flying, but a flood of newly tradable stock could prove stronger than the next launch catalyst.

title: SpaceX Gains 1.5% Before Falcon 9's 104th Launch
